frontier.hypothesis: Reading the sched2 tiebreak in a THIRD form — using a permuter-directed rewrite of the loop that changes how many block-0-live values the addu $21 chain touches — could shorten the sll's downstream dependency chain enough to demote its INSN_PRIORITY below 1 (currently equal to move16), moving the tie to a different tiebreak axis.
frontier.mechanism: s3 measured INSN_PRIORITY(sll)==INSN_PRIORITY(move16)==1, tie broken by INSN_LUID. If sll's priority could be reduced to 0 while move16 stays at 1, the priority tiebreak wouldn't fire and sched2 would emit in priority order (move16 first). sched.c INSN_PRIORITY is longest downstream dependence chain; sll feeds sll->addu $1->lw $20->addu $21(delay). If addu $21's dependence on sll's chain could be broken (e.g. by expressing s5 through a value NOT derived from *(base+v1)), the chain length drops.
frontier.next_probe: Read sched.c compute_priority + downstream chain traversal to identify exactly what edge to sever. Then attempt a C spelling where s5's ADDU sources bypass the sll->lw chain (e.g. compute s5 from a preloaded value or via a route that doesn't extend the sll chain). Must be pure C, must retain the delay-slot fill of addu $21 into the beqz.
